concept.name: Protocol revenue
concept.definition: Protocol revenue is the portion of the fees a protocol collects that is kept by the protocol entity itself — flowing to its treasury or governance token holders — as distinct from fees passed through to liquidity providers or other suppliers.
concept.intuition: If fees are the till, protocol revenue is what the house actually keeps after paying the market makers who stocked the shelves.
concept.mechanics: Using DefiLlama's taxonomy: total fees = all value collected from users; revenue = fees kept by the protocol = protocol revenue (to treasury/team) + holders revenue (distributed to token holders via buybacks, burns or dividends); the remainder is supply-side revenue to LPs/lenders. Only the kept fraction represents income attributable to the protocol and its token.
concept.formula: Revenue = ProtocolRevenue + HoldersRevenue; Fees = Revenue + SupplySideRevenue.
concept.failure_modes: Revenue funded by unsustainable incentive cycles or one-off events (liquidation spikes) is not recurring income; comparing revenue across protocols without distinguishing holders vs treasury vs supply-side fractions invites apples-to-oranges valuation errors.
concept.misconceptions: Fees are not revenue — a DEX's 0.3% swap fee mostly belongs to LPs, and only the protocol's cut (if any) is revenue. TVL is not revenue either; it is capital parked, not income earned.
concept.example: If a lending protocol collects $1M of borrower interest in a day and keeps a 10% reserve factor, its daily revenue is $100k — split between treasury accrual and any buybacks for token holders — while $900k is supply-side revenue to lenders.
